title: THE HUDDLE. Issue 01. Jun 30th (includes the Market integrity report)
summary: Monthly letter for June 2026. Contains Limitless's own market integrity report: one or more on-chain actors used Morpho flash loans to become the only liquidity provider in AMM (FPMM) markets, traded against their own liquidity, withdrew the liquidity with the fees and repaid the loan inside one transaction. Limitless calls it abuse of the points program and the Terms, says it was found after a community report plus internal analysis, banned the accounts, cut their points, stripped the volume from public market data and added monitoring. Also reports June launches (Packs, user-generated markets, self-trade prevention, NAVI, Clarence Seedorf, $1M World Cup challenge) and a new written policy on prohibited markets (assassination, harm, terrorism) with no link to a policy page.
key_facts: Flash-loan wash volume: $2.7B notional across more than 1,000 trades.

Wallets involved: 309 wallets/profiles (report header), listed in a linked Notion page that did not render for automated fetching. Actor described as 'on-chain actor(s)'; the letter says Limitless identified the accounts, issued bans and cut Limitless points rewards.
Example transaction: 0xe19542e6b7f50638eea02c43eca08f888f0e3b8848f55af727f92243caed443c (Base).
Example cycle: flash loan about $1,121,110 USDC from Morpho; buy $9,999 (fee 39.996 USDC); sell $9,919 (fee 39.836 USDC); LP fee recovery 79.82 USDC; loan repaid.
Root cause stated by Limitless: the same address could be both LP and trader, and fees were recoverable by the LP.
Dune tables published for data reporters: dune.limitless_exchange.dataset_flashloan_wallets and dune.limitless_exchange.dataset_flashloan_daily_volume; SQL template filters 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-01.

Opening paragraph separately says a single account manufacturing fake volume was found and all of it removed from public stats. The letter does not say whether this is the same finding as the 309 flash-loan wallets.
User-generated markets beta: 162 creators, 1,611 markets, $2.2M volume in first month.
Describes Limitless as a hybrid CLOB/AMM marketplace. The reported abuse concerns AMM (FPMM) markets only; the letter says nothing about wash trading on the order book.
caveats: Does not restate earlier public figures (April record month, $3.9B cumulative, Season 3 $4B) and does not say whether the banned wallets received the Season 3 airdrop that opened on 2026-05-27. The only date range given is the SQL filter.

title: What Is Market Manipulation? Types, Examples, & Staying Safe
author: Michael McAllister
summary: Limitless's own educational post. Defines market manipulation, spoofing and layering, and wash trading (simultaneous buying and selling to fake volume with no change of ownership), says US law has banned wash trading since the 1930s, cites studies claiming most bitcoin volume on some exchanges was fake, lists penalties and laws (Exchange Act s.9, CEA, EU MAR, FCA). Claims on-chain recording and community auditing protect against wash trading and spoofing.
caveats: Describes no internal surveillance. Nine months later Limitless disclosed $2.7B of wash volume on its own AMM markets (S001).

A code comment says taker fees swept to the treasury are forwarded in full to traders as maker rebates, LP rewards and creator fees. The campaign is run by 'Limitless' with no legal entity named.
